title: Confession IDs are truncated SHA-256 of content and timestamp
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/confessions.py
Perspective: security (privacy)

Spec 18.10 is an anonymous board. Example ids look random (8a4f2b).
DeadDropResource uses secrets.token_hex(3).

_generate_id() (lines 42-45) does
sha256(f"{content}:{timestamp}").hexdigest()[:6]. timestamp is the
SenML bt (client-supplied) or receive time. _unique_id() only
suffixes on in-store collision.

Impact:
- ID is a fingerprint of content+bt; a guess of the text can be
  verified without reading the body from another replica
- identical content+bt on an empty board yields a stable, predictable
  Location-Path
- unlinkability fails for the same confession stored on multiple
  nodes

Acceptance: allocate confession ids from a CSPRNG (same 6-hex form)
with collision retry, not from content hash.
close_reason: Confession IDs now come from secrets.token_hex(3) with in-store collision retry, matching DeadDrop. Content/timestamp SHA-256 fingerprinting is gone. Tests pin format, unlinkability of identical payloads, independent-hash non-match, collision retry, and POST Location-Path.
